newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins edge down, profit-taking continues.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins edge down, profit-taking continues.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged down on Friday on continued profit-taking after recent strong gains, and dealers said U.S. producer price data, which some said should have been friendly to the market, failed to lend support.
"Russia seems pressured compared with the rest of emerging markets," one dealer said. "MinFins eased further on profit-taking after U.S. figures."
The U.S. Labor Department reported on Friday the June Producer Price Index (PPI) fell 0.1 percent, pointing to what traders said would be further stability in official U.S. interest rates.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected an unchanged reading on June PPI.
MinFins, along with other emerging market debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.

"The market seems not to have a clear idea whether the data is good or not," Avtobank dealer Ivan Kuznetsov said. "Prices have been fluctuating the whole day but downside prevailed after the week-long rise."

MinFins set records last Wednesday when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) left interest rates unchanged at a regular meeting. Prices had set new consecutive records for a whole week until Wednesday, when the profit-taking set in.
